semantic_argument: FreyPackage is a complete structure whose constructor requires each data field and proofs of its properties; it is not a placeholder object returned by a data sorry.

Under p>0 and a^p+b^p=c^p, if a prime divides both a and c, it divides b^p and hence b, contradicting gcd(a,b)=1; the same argument applies to b and c. Thus storing just one coprime pair does not enlarge the admissible packages. The source lemmas gcdab_eq_gcdac, hgcdac, and hgcdbc provide the corresponding proofs.

The ZMod fields express integer congruences and support negative integers, matching the source requirement that a,b,c are integers; they do not impose an unwarranted positivity requirement on all three.

FermatLastTheoremFor p states that the equation at that exponent has no solution in nonzero natural numbers. The formal proof first obtains a natural-number counterexample, converts it to integers, removes common factors, adjusts the position of the even term and the overall sign, and finally constructs an actual FreyPackage.
Nonempty FreyPackage expresses the existence of a structure satisfying every field constraint, matching the bound lemma's assertion that there exists a Frey package.

FreyPackage in the declaration is not parameterized by the input p, and the conclusion does not state ∃P, P.p=p. The declaration therefore does not express the stronger conclusion that the exponent is preserved. The actual proof ultimately constructs the structure using the input p, but this does not mean that the public declaration guarantees P.p=p. The current source conclusion does not explicitly add this endpoint, so it is not used as a basis for a negative label here; the construction for a given p in the source proof prose is retained as a scope note.

Neither extracted graph contains galoisRep, and the retained local definition values contain no data sorry. This case does not have the previous case's missing binding to the natural Galois representation.
